messages.subject: part5 person summary output
parts:
Dear Vincent, 

Thank you for having the new update! 

I ran the GGIR script with the updated version, and I got the desired outputs for part5 day summary. However, when it came to the part 5 person summary output, it came out as one column of data..  

the script that I used to run the dataset is below.. and the output that I got is attached.. 
Just wanted to check if I needed to add something in the script? Or wanted to check what might be the cause of this since I had managed to run the previous versions fine.. 

Script: 

path = setwd("/Users/GGIR")
medal <- paste0(path, "/Dataset") 
output_results <- paste0(path, "/Outputs") 

# modify according to your analysis
part5dur <- c(1)
part2mvpadur <- c(1, 3, 5)
part1mode <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
part5mode <- c(2, 4, 5)

# version 2.0
files <- list.files(medal)
f <- files[1]

for (f in files) {
  n <- gsub(".csv", "", f)
  dir.create(paste0(path, "/Outputs/", n))
  test <- tryCatch(
  {g.shell.GGIR(#=======================================
             # INPUT NEEDED:
             mode=part1mode,# change if not need all 5 parts
             datadir= paste0(medal, "/", f),
             outputdir= paste0(path, "/Outputs/", n),
             #-------------------------------
             f0=1, f1=1,
             # Part 1:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
             windowsizes = c(5, 900, 3600), desiretz = "Asia/Shanghai",
             studyname = c("Dataset"), chunksize = 0.5,
             do.enmo = TRUE, do.anglez=TRUE,
             do.hfen = FALSE, do.hfenplus = FALSE,
             do.cal = TRUE, use.temp = FALSE,
             minloadcrit = 100, # default = 72, may need to change later
             printsummary = TRUE, print.filename = TRUE,
             overwrite = TRUE,
             selectdaysfile = c(),  # check how to use this argument
             dayborder = 0, dynrange = c(), # default = 8g
             
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2:
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 2, # may use = 3 (only select most active n days)
             hrs.del.start = 0, hrs.del.end = 0,
             maxdur = 50,   # may need to change if processing all 140 datasets
             includedaycrit = 16,
             M5L5res = 10,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qlevels = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
             qwindow=c(0,24),
             ilevels = c(0, 35,200, 707, 100000),
             mvpathreshold =c(200),
             boutcriter = 0.8,
             ndayswindow= 7, # used only when strategy = 3
             idloc = 2, # double check if can use 1
             do.imp = TRUE, # may need to change later
             storefolderstructure = TRUE,
             epochvalues2csv = TRUE,
             mvpadur = part2mvpadur,
             bout.metric = 4,
             closedbout=FALSE,
             # IVIS_windowsize_minutes and IVIS_epochsize_seconds use default 60m /3600s
             
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 3:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Sleep detection
             timethreshold= c(5),        anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = TRUE,       acc.metric="ENMO",
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 4: (omit for now)
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Integrating sleep log (if available) with sleep detection
             # storing day and person specific summaries of sleep
             excludefirstlast = FALSE,
             includenightcrit = 16,
             #def.noc.sleep = c(),
             loglocation= c(),
             #outliers.only = TRUE,
             #criterror = 4,
             #relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
             #sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
             #colid=1,
             #coln1=2,
             #do.visual = TRUE,
             nnights = c(),

             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5:
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             #-------------------------------
             threshold.lig = c(35), threshold.mod = c(200),  threshold.vig = c(707),
             boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(part5dur), boutdur.lig = c(part5dur),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(part5dur),   timewindow = c("MM", "WW"),
             #-----------------------------------
             # Report generation
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Generating reports based on meta-data
             do.report=part5mode,
             visualreport=TRUE,  dofirstpage = TRUE,
             viewingwindow=1
  )}, error = function(e) e)
  
  if(inherits(test, "error")) { 
    print(paste0("File error in ", f))
    next()
  }
}

Thanks in advanced!  

Regards, 
Claire

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] part5 person summary output
parts:
Hi Claire,

Does this happen to all your files? Possibly R transposes a single row output matrix into a column matrix. So, we would have to investigate when and where that happens and stop it from happening. If you are a software developer, feel free to submit a pull request, if not I am happy to do this as a paid consultancy.

For others reading this - I suspect Claire wants to generate a report per participant in patient-oriented setting. This is not the way you should normally be using g.shell.GGIR in research. Instead specify argument datadir as the directory where your data is located and avoid using the loop.

Thanks, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
https://accelting.com/

This issue should be fixed now in the development version of GGIR on GitHub.

To install this version do:
library("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR")
library("GGIR")

Thanks for reporting it, Vincent
